Statement-only numerical definitions and objects (addendum)

For the numerical tail assertions (IR4,CEN1,OBS1), define V={nu>=1:r*nu in Irr}.
Define P(X)=1+X+sum_{nu in V}alpha_nu X^nu in F_p[X].
In increasing order of nu in V, alpha_nu is the unique coefficient making
[X^nu]logP=0. Other coefficients are zero except constant1 and X coefficient1.
The formal logarithm here is needed only through max(V), which is <p.
This definition of P is used for the listed nonadmissible r as well.
The specified expansion data (the reference eq:tail-data) are:
H_b(T)=T*P(b^(2r+1)*T^(2r)) modT^p, H_inf(T)=T^(2r+1), s=p^2*n,
with nonzero integer n; the reported failures use n=1.
Projection residues with augmentation s and expansions H are defined by
F3's transform after adding s/p-1 to each entry of varrho_e(z).
Thus the failing-cell assertion concerns the exact congruence in F2 evaluated
on the projection residues specified by these H. No method of verification
or favorable verdict is supplied here.

At p=103 the assertions use r=1,2,3,4 and the only irregular half-index12;
at p=131 use r=1 and half-index11; at p=157 use r=1 with half-indices31,55.
IR4 uses p=37,59,67 with half-indices16,22,29 and r=1.

For prime-count assertions (PC1), for each p in {11,13} and cutoff x,
N_p(x)=#{rational primes ell<=x: ell!=p, ell=1 modp, a prime ideal q|ell
is principal and its coordinates satisfy TheoremC(a)}.
The field class numbers h_K at p11,p13 are asserted to be1.
The zero-triple count for p13 is the same enumeration with only c3=c5=c7=0;
there is no choice-dependent nonzero-frequency claim.
The density comparison is pi(x)*(p+1)/p^((p-3)/2), rounded to one decimal.
The two tables from the current assertions follow.

Additional census assertion: among2259primes7<=p<20000,900areirregular;
r_p=1,2,...,8 frequencies1602,283,224,67,59,6,16,2. Exactly657have e(p)>p+5.
The ratio is approximately0.291. The heuristic limiting comparison is
1-exp(-1/3) approximately0.283, explicitly conditional on independent
irregular-pair events of probability1/p (not a theorem about convergence).

DET1 mathematical object: the following is an 11-by-11 integer array v.
Rows are i=0,...,10; columns j=0,...,10, in that order. Its group matrix
is (v[(i-k)mod11][(j-l)mod11]) for row(i,j),column(k,l), the group determinant
definition in the packet. Assertions: augmentation11, determinant11^15*77419,
all121entries have absolute value below10^36. The vector is data needed to
state this finite assertion; no author program or verification output follows.
